arxiv-1912-03763.title: Regionalised heat demand and power-to-heat capacities in Germany – An open data set for assessing renewable energy integration Journal: Applied Energy
arxiv-1912-03763.creator: Wilko Heitkoetter, Wided Medjroubi, Thomas Vogt, Carsten Agert
arxiv-1912-03763.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Wilko Heitkoetter, Wided Medjroubi, Thomas Vogt, Carsten Agert. Higher shares of fluctuating generation from renewable energy sources (RES) in the power system lead to an increase of grid balancing demand. One approach for avoiding RES curtailment, is to use excess electricity feed-in for heating applications. To assess in which regions power-to-heat (PtH) technologies can contribute to RES integration, detailed data on the spatial distribution of the heat demand are needed.

arxiv-2108-06953.title: Uniform Function Estimators in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
arxiv-2108-06953.creator: Paul Dommel, Alois Pichler
arxiv-2108-06953.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Paul Dommel, Alois Pichler. This paper addresses the problem of regression to reconstruct functions, which are observed with superimposed errors at random locations. We address the problem in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. It is demonstrated that the estimator, which is often derived by employing Gaussian random fields, converges in the mean norm of the reproducing kernel Hilbert space to the conditional expectation and this implies local and uniform convergence of this function estimator.

arxiv-2201-08694.title: Genuine multipartite entanglement of quantum states in the multiple-copy scenario
arxiv-2201-08694.creator: Carlos Palazuelos, Julio I. de Vicente
arxiv-2201-08694.description: Abstract Genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) is considered a powerful form of entanglement since it corresponds to those states that are not biseparable, i.e. a mixture of partially separable states across different bipartitions of the parties. In this work we study this phenomenon in the multiple-copy regime, where many perfect copies of a given state can be produced and controlled.

arxiv-2202-01795.title: A Pair of Early- and Late-Forming Galaxy Cluster Samples: a Novel Way of Studying Halo Assembly Bias Assisted by a Constrained Simulation
arxiv-2202-01795.creator: Yen-Ting Lin, Hironao Miyatake, Hong Guo, Yi-Kuan Chiang, Kai-Feng Chen, Ting-Wen Lan, Yu-Yen Chang
arxiv-2202-01795.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yen-Ting Lin, Hironao Miyatake, Hong Guo, Yi-Kuan Chiang, Kai-Feng Chen, Ting-Wen Lan, Yu-Yen Chang. The halo assembly bias, a phenomenon referring to dependencies of the large-scale bias of a dark matter halo other than its mass, is a fundamental property of the standard cosmological model. First discovered in 2005 from the Millennium Run simulation, it has been proven very difficult to be detected observationally, with only a few convincing claims of detection so far.

arxiv-2209-00621.title: Combinatorial decomposition theorem for Hitchin systems via zonotopes
arxiv-2209-00621.creator: Mirko Mauri, Luca Migliorini and Roberto Pagaria
arxiv-2209-00621.description: Abstract . We determine the summands of the decomposition theorem for the Hitchin system for GL n \operatorname{GL}_{n} , in arbitrary degree, over the locus of reduced spectral curves. The key ingredient is an equivariant formula for lattice point counts in graphical zonotopes. 1. Introduction Intersection cohomology is a topological invariant well-adapted to investigate the symmetries of singular spaces.

arxiv-2311-06210.title: Optimal Cooperative Multiplayer Learning Bandits with Noisy Rewards and No Communication chang314@g.ucla.edu terrylu@princeton.edu
arxiv-2311-06210.creator: William Chang, Yuanhao Lu
arxiv-2311-06210.description: Abstract We consider a cooperative multiplayer bandit learning problem where the players are only allowed to agree on a strategy beforehand, but cannot communicate during the learning process. In this problem, each player simultaneously selects an action. Based on the actions selected by all players, the team of players receives a reward.

arxiv-2401-04858.title: User Embedding Model for Personalized Language Prompting
arxiv-2401-04858.creator: Sumanth Doddapaneni, Krishna Sayana , Ambarish Jash, Sukhdeep Sodhi, Dima Kuzmin
arxiv-2401-04858.description: Abstract Modeling long user histories plays a pivotal role in enhancing recommendation systems, allowing to capture users’ evolving preferences, resulting in more precise and personalized recommendations. In this study, we tackle the challenges of modeling long user histories for preference understanding in natural language.

arxiv-2409-04999.title: Visual Grounding with Multi-modal Conditional Adaptation
arxiv-2409-04999.creator: Ruilin Yao, Shengwu Xiong, Yichen Zhao, Yi Rong
arxiv-2409-04999.description: Abstract . Visual grounding is the task of locating objects specified by natural language expressions. Existing methods extend generic object detection frameworks to tackle this task. They typically extract visual and textual features separately using independent visual and textual encoders, then fuse these features in a multi-modal decoder for final prediction. However, visual grounding presents unique challenges.

arxiv-2410-05244.title: Simulation of the High Mach Number Motion for Bubble Collapse in a Compressible Euler Fluid using Basilisk
arxiv-2410-05244.creator: Daniels Krimans, Steven J. Ruuth, Seth Putterman
arxiv-2410-05244.description: Abstract We examine an extreme case of experimentally realizable sonoluminescence, where spherical cavities have an initial radius that is 10 10 to 20 20 times their ambient radius and change their radius by a factor of over 100 100 during the collapse.

arxiv-2508-08018.title: Integrality and Specialized Symmetric Functions
arxiv-2508-08018.creator: Allan Berele
arxiv-2508-08018.description: Abstract 1 Introduction In [ 3 ] , together with S. Catoiu, we introduced the specialized symmetric functions. These can be regarded from two points of view, either symmetric function theory or trace idenitities. Given (d)=(d_{1},\ldots,d_{k}) we defined the specialized power function as p^{(d)}_{n}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{k}) to be d_{1}x_{1}^{n}+\cdots+d_{k}x_{k}^{n} .

The image processing requirements for reliable individual recognition under these circumstances are computationally intensive since local featu

pmc-11437100.title: Exploring and validating the necroptotic gene regulation and related lncRNA mechanisms in colon adenocarcinoma based on multi-dimensional data
pmc-11437100.creator: Weili Wang, Yi Liu, Ziqi Wang, Xiaoning Tan, Xiaolan Jian, Zhen Zhang
pmc-11437100.description: Necroptosis is intimately associated with the initiation and progression of colon adenocarcinoma (COAD). However, studies on necroptosis-related genes (NRGs) and the regulating long non-coding RNAs (NRGlncRNAs) in the context of COAD are limited. We retrieved the cancer genome atlas (TCGA) to collect datasets of NRGs and NRGlncRNAs on COAD patients.

pmc-11490257.title: Efficacy and Safety of Jiuxin Pill in the Treatment of Patients with Stable Angina Pectoris: A Protocol for a Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Clinical Trial
pmc-11490257.creator: Tongzuo Liu, Jingyi Zhang, Zhiqiang Zhao, Yingfei Bi, Ying Zheng, Shuai Wang, Xiaohua Dai, Jun Li, Qian Lin, Daimei Ni, Chenglong Wang, Jianguang Wu, Yitao Xue, Mingjun Zhu, Xianliang Wang, Jingyuan Mao
pmc-11490257.description: BackgroundStable angina pectoris (SAP), as a common type of coronary heart disease (CHD), is characterized by transient retrosternal squeezing pain or suffocation induced by exercise, mood swings, or other stress. Most patients with stable angina pectoris do not benefit from interventional therapy and medication, so optimizing treatment plans has important clinical significance.

pmc-11621516.title: Adhesive interactions within microbial consortia can be differentiated at the single-cell level through expansion microscopy
pmc-11621516.creator: Pu-Ting Dong, Wenyuan Shi, Xuesong He, Gary G. Borisy
pmc-11621516.description: SignificanceA single-cell understanding of microbe–microbe interactions is critical for unraveling the organization and dynamics of microbial communities. Through an unconventional application of expansion microscopy, we oppose the adhesive force holding microbes together by an expansion force pulling them apart, resulting in microbial separation dependent on the strength of microbial adhesion.

pmc-12599085.title: Molecular characteristics and regulatory effects of dwarfing Rht genes in Triticum aestivum L
pmc-12599085.creator: Ying run Wang, Jia Shi, Yi yang He, Yu lu Tao, Lan tian Ren, Qing qin Shao, Xiang Chen, Zi feng Wu, Jin cai Li, Jia cheng Zheng
pmc-12599085.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundApplication of Rht dwarfing genes has significantly enhanced plant lodging resistance and harvest index. However, the numerous members of Rht genes, particularly newly cloned genes in recent years, remain poorly understood in integrated analysis of their expression patterns under stress conditions, allelic interaction effects, and molecular regulatory mechanisms, these limit our comprehensive exploration of Rht gene regulatory network, and hinder the potential application in wheat genetic improvement.ResultsThis study comprehensively analyzed the characteristics of Rht family members.

pmc-13052604.title: Anti-tumor Effect of Glycopeptides with Different Morphologies
pmc-13052604.creator: Qi He, Lintong Yao, Rongying Liu, Lin Yin, Guoliang Tang, Guang Yang, Zhijun Shi, Guosong Chen
pmc-13052604.description: Tumor progression is intricately associated with dysregulated extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Supramolecular fibers composed of biomolecules exhibit structural and functional characteristics reminiscent of the native ECM. Leveraging this similarity, the construction of such fibers within the pericellular space may reconstruct the dysregulated ECM and act as a promising anticancer strategy, by remodeling the interactions between tumor cells and their microenvironment.

pmc-13104482.title: In silico and in vitro insights into the wound-healing potential of syringic acid: protective and regenerative effects on human fibroblasts
pmc-13104482.creator: Ufuk Okkay, İlkin Kazimov, Irmak Ferah Okkay, Azizeh Shadidizaji, Mehmet Ali Yoruk, Murat Ozdemir, Fatih Burak Yildiz, Fatma Yesilyurt, Mustafa Ozkaraca, Ahmet Hacimuftuoglu
pmc-13104482.description: This study aimed to investigate the wound-healing potential of syringic acid (SA) through integrated in silico and in vitro approaches using human dermal fibroblasts (HDFs). Network pharmacology analysis identified myeloperoxidase (MPO), a key enzyme involved in oxidative stress and inflammation, as a primary target of SA. Computational predictions also indicated favorable pharmacokinetic and ADMET properties.

pmc-13188976.title: The sustainability of the healthcare: a cross-sectional study among Italian JCI-accredited hospitals
pmc-13188976.creator: Pier Mario Perrone, Martina Lauria, Fabrizio Tediosi, Silvana Castaldi
pmc-13188976.description: BackgroundThe health sector is characterized by dual aspects in relation to climate change and its impact on human health. To consider firstly the treatment of resulting health problems; and secondly the representation of environmental impact as a primary cause. Consequently, a number of certification bodies have indicated their intention to incorporate sustainability criteria into their certification processes.

pmc-13426870.title: Dynamic Interfacial pH Stabilization and (002) Oriented Deposition Enabled by Histidine‐Induced Solid Electrolyte Interphase for Highly Reversible Zn Anodes
pmc-13426870.creator: Qi Liu, Yimin Chen, Jianwei Lu, Xiangqun Zhuge, Xiyuan Zhong, Huaichong Sun, Yibing Li, Zhihong Luo, Kun Luo, Weiwei Lei, Dan Liu, Anjun Hu, Aijing Ma
pmc-13426870.description: Aqueous zinc batteries hold great promise for large‐scale energy storage due to their high energy density, safety, and cost‐effectiveness. However, the intrinsic thermodynamic instability of zinc drives inevitable HER, leading to interfacial accumulation of OH− that significantly exacerbates dendrite growth and “dead zinc” formation.

pmc-13431683.title: Increased medial anterior tibial translation and reduced tibiofemoral rotation are observed during weight bearing in anterior cruciate ligament‐deficient knees: A paired within‐subject imaging analysis
pmc-13431683.creator: Riccardo D'Ambrosi, Stefano Fusco, Filippo Rinciari, Pietro Marchetti, Domenico Albano, Salvatore Gitto, Luca Maria Sconfienza
pmc-13431683.description: PurposeTo evaluate the effect of weight‐bearing computed tomography (WBCT) on knee kinematics in anterior cruciate ligament (ACL)‐deficient knees using a within‐subject comparison between WBCT and non–weight‐bearing conditions (NWBCT).MethodsThis was a prospective within‐subject observational imaging study. Patients with chronic ACL deficiency underwent both WBCT and NWBCT cone‐beam computed tomography scans of the same knee.

pmc-13458783.title: Interpretable white-box modeling for nitrogen storage in metal–organic frameworks
pmc-13458783.creator: Arefeh Naghizadeh, Fahimeh Hadavimoghaddam, Meftah Ali Abuswer, Ahmad Mohaddespour, Abdolhossein Hemmati-Sarapardeh, Saeid Atashrouz
pmc-13458783.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The efficient removal of low-concentration nitrogen (N2) is a critical and challenging task in the industrial production of high-purity oxygen (O2), particularly in air separation processes and in natural gas purification for generating high-purity methane (CH4). In this work, three advanced modeling techniques, namely the group method of data handling (GMDH), gene expression programming (GEP), and genetic programming (GP) were applied to develop user-friendly mathematical correlations for predicting nitrogen storage capacity of MOFs. A broad dataset of 3073 laboratory measurements was employed.

pmc-13553675.title: Long-term memory speeds encoding, independently of attention
pmc-13553675.creator: Abigail C Wyllie, Claudia C von Bastian, Alon Zivony
pmc-13553675.description: Recent studies suggest that familiar objects benefit from faster working memory (WM) encoding – the transformation of fragile perceptual representations into durable WM representations. This observation led contemporary WM models to postulate a long-term memory (LTM) “template-matching” mechanism, which speeds standard encoding processes. However, faster encoding may also be caused by higher attentional priority for familiar objects.
